title: About Form 706, United States Estate (and Generation-Skipping Transfer) Tax Return | Internal Revenue Service
text: Skip to main content About Form 706, United States Estate (and Generation-Skipping Transfer) Tax Return More In Forms and Instructions Current year Prior year Accessible eBooks Browser-friendly forms and publications Mobile-friendly forms Post release changes to forms Order forms and publications Help with forms and instructions Comment on tax forms and publications The executor of a decedent's estate uses Form 706 to figure the estate tax imposed by Chapter 11 of the Internal Revenue Code. Form 706 is also used to figure the generation-skipping transfer (GST) tax imposed by Chapter 13 on direct skips. Current revision Form 706 PDF Instructions for Form 706 ( Print version PDF ) Recent developments Estate tax closing letter fee reduced to $56 effective May 21, 2025 -- 23-MAY-2025 Schedules Schedule A (Form 706), Real Estate If the total gross estate contains any real estate, use this schedule to report assets from real estate. Schedule A (Form 706) PDF Schedule B (Form 706), Stocks and Bonds If the total gross estate contains any stocks or bonds, use this schedule to report assets from stocks or bonds. Schedule B (Form 706) PDF Schedule C (Form 706), Mortgages, Notes, and Cash If the total gross estate contains any mortgages, notes, or cash, use this schedule to report assets from mortgages, notes, or cash. Schedule C (Form 706) PDF Schedule D (Form 706), Insurance on the Decedent’s Life If there was any insurance on the decedent’s life, whether or not included in the gross estate, use this schedule to report every insurance policy. Schedule D (Form 706) PDF Schedule E (Form 706), Jointly Owned Property If the decedent owned any joint property at the time of death, and whether or not the decedent’s interest is includable in the gross estate, use this schedule to report the property. Schedule E (Form 706) PDF Schedule F (Form 706), Other Miscellaneous Property Not Reportable Under Any Other Schedule Use this schedule to include all items that must be included in the gross estate that are not reported on any other schedule. Schedule F (Form 706) PDF Schedule G (Form 706), Transfers During the Decedent’s Lifetime If the decedent made any transfers under sections 2035(a), 2035(b), 2036, 2037, or 2038, use this schedule to report the transfers. Schedule G (Form 706) PDF Schedule H (Form 706), Powers of Appointment If the decedent ever possessed, exercised, or released any general power of appointment, use this schedule to report the powers of appointment. Schedule H (Form 706) PDF Schedule I (Form 706), Annuities If the decedent, immediately before death, received any type of annuity, use this schedule to report the annuities. Schedule I (Form 706) PDF Schedule J (Form 706), Funeral Expenses and Expenses Incurred in Administering Property Subject to Claims Use this schedule to itemize funeral and property expenses during administration that are subject to claims. Schedule J (Form 706) PDF Schedule K (Form 706), Debts, Mortgages, and Liens If deductions are claimed for debts of the decedent and mortgages and liens, use this schedule to report those deductions. Schedule K (Form 706) PDF Schedule L (Form 706), Net Losses During Administration and Expenses Incurred in Administering Property Not Subject to Claims If deductions are claimed for net losses and property expenses during administration that are not subject to claims, use this schedule to report those deductions. Schedule L (Form 706) PDF Schedule M (Form 706), Bequests, etc., to Surviving Spouse Use this schedule to claim marital deductions for certain property interests that pass from the decedent to the surviving spouse. Schedule M (Form 706) PDF Schedule O (Form 706), Charitable, Public, and Similar Gifts and Bequests Use this schedule to claim a deduction for charitable, public, and similar gifts and bequests. Schedule O (Form 706) PDF Schedule P (Form 706), Credit for Certain Foreign Taxes Use this schedule to claim a credit for certain foreign taxes when authorized under a statue or a treaty. Schedule P (Form 706) PDF Schedule PC (Form 706), Protective Claim for Refund Use this schedule to file a section 2053 protective claim for refund by estates of decedents who died after 2011. The schedule also serves to inform the IRS when the contingency leading to the protective claim for refund is resolved and the refund due the estate is finalized. Schedule PC (Form 706) PDF Schedule Q (Form 706), Credit for Tax on Prior Transfers Use this schedule to claim a credit for a prior transfer. Schedule Q (Form 706) PDF Schedule R (Form 706), Generation-Skipping Transfer Tax Use this schedule to figure the generation-skipping transfer (GST) tax that is payable by the estate. Schedule R (Form 706) PDF Schedule R-1 (Form 706), Generation-Skipping Transfer Tax Use this schedule to figure the generation-skipping transfer (GST) tax that is payable by certain trusts that are includible in the gross estate. Schedule R-1 (Form 706) PDF Schedule T (Form 706), Section 2032A Property Valuation Use this schedule to make an election to value certain farm and closely held business property at special value. Schedule T (Form 706) PDF Schedule U (Form 706), Qualified Conservation Easement Exclusion Use this schedule to make an election to exclude a portion of the value of land that is subject to qualified conservation easement under section 2031(c). Schedule U (Form 706) PDF Schedule W (Form 706), Continuation Schedule for Form 706 Schedules Use this schedule as needed to list additional assets or deductions.
